archetype.name: Play-In Team (turnover-driven)
archetype.definition: A roughly league-average team on both ends that wins the possession battle with ball security and forced turnovers but gives away the paint and the glass, which leaves it around .500 and in the play-in mix.

report.headline: Elite turnover margin, leaky paint: a .500 team whose 3-4 start fits
report.take:
Atlanta is seven games into 2026-27 and is almost exactly what its numbers say: a middle team. The Net Rtg of 0.9 ranks 15th, the offense is 15th and the defense 17th, and the site has the Hawks 16th of 30. The 3-4 record is one win short of what the margin implies (W vs Pt Diff of -1, 4 wins by differential), so the record isn't hiding a much better or worse team. This comes after a 46-36 season with a top-10 defense, so the open question is whether that defense slipped or is just being measured over a handful of games.

The identity is the turnover battle. A 12.3 TOV % (4th) and a 16.4 Opp TOV % (2nd) mean Atlanta gets far more shots than its opponents. That is what keeps an ordinary shooting team afloat. The Hawks take a lot of threes (44.8 3PA Rate, 11th) but are making only 32.8% of them (22nd), and with a 23.4 FT Rate (26th) they almost never get easy points at the line. The free-throw problem is structural: last year's FT Rate was the same 23.4. The three-point slump probably isn't. This group shot 37.1% a year ago, and a deep-shooting backcourt led by Nickeil Alexander-Walker (22 threes, +18.2 On-Off) and Aaron Wiggins (62.7 TS %) should pull that number up.

The numbers hide some things. The +6 point differential leans heavily on one game, the 128-81 demolition of Charlotte. Over the last five games Atlanta is 1-4 and has been outscored by 9.6 a game, more than ten points worse than its season average. The defense is also living on opponents missing threes: an Opp 3P % of 32 (7th) against 35.5 last year. Underneath, the rim defense is the worst in the league by volume. Opponents take 37% of their shots within four feet (30th), 7 points above the league average, and convert 70.4% of them (25th). The frontcourt grades D-, Jock Landale is out, and the bigs got 355 minutes in total against 773 for the backcourt. Opposing power forwards are pulling down 14.57 rebounds a game, 29th, and 3.23 above their own norms. When the opponents' three-point luck evens out, that paint problem will cost real points.

Where it's heading: the offense should rise toward its history as the threes start falling, and the defense should sag as opponents' threes do the same. Those two roughly cancel, which points to a team hovering around .500 for most of the year. Whether it ends up a few games above or below depends on whether the frontcourt gets healthier and bigger, and on Jalen Johnson (6th of 86 on the SF tab, day-to-day) staying on the floor.

strengths.title: Winning the turnover battle
strengths.body: Atlanta protects the ball (12.3 TOV %, 4th) and forces mistakes at nearly the league's best rate (16.4 Opp TOV %, 2nd), 2.4 points above the league average. Ball security has been a Hawks trait for years, and last season's 12.3 TOV % was identical. The forcing side is newer and partly sample-driven. Even if it fades toward last year's 13.9, the extra possessions are the main reason a poor-shooting team is still above water on Net Rtg.

strengths.title: Guard depth that can shoot
strengths.body: The backcourt grades B+ and carries the scoring. Alexander-Walker leads the team in points with a +18.2 On-Off, Wiggins is at 62.7 TS %, and Dyson Daniels ranks 11th of 110 on the SG tab without needing the ball. Point guards against Atlanta have managed just 10.29 points a game, fewest in the league. This is the most durable part of the roster.

strengths.title: Three-point shooting due to rise
strengths.body: The Hawks are shooting 32.8% from three, 1.9 below the league, while still taking threes at an above-average rate. The same core shot 37.1% last season. A rebound toward the mid-30s would push an offense that ranks 15th toward the top third without any change in approach.

concerns.title: No resistance at the rim
concerns.body: Opponents take 37% of their shots at the rim, last in the league and 7 points above average, and they finish 70.4% of them (25th). The D- frontcourt, Landale's absence and heavy small-ball minutes are the likely cause. That makes this structural rather than noise until the size situation changes.

concerns.title: Defense propped up by opponents' misses
concerns.body: An Opp 3P % of 32 ranks 7th, 2.9 below the league and well under last year's 35.5. Opponents' three-point shooting is the noisiest defensive number there is. Once it normalizes, the rim leak turns a 17th-ranked defense into a below-average one.

concerns.title: The margin is one blowout deep
concerns.body: The season's +6 differential includes a 128-81 rout of Charlotte. Since then Atlanta is 1-4 and has been outscored by 9.6 a game. The rebounding hasn't held up either, with a REB % of 47.4 (24th). The recent stretch is closer to the team's floor than its true level, but it isn't a fluke.

trend.note: A 2-0 start, both road wins including the 47-point Charlotte rout, has given way to a 1-4 stretch in which Atlanta scored 5.49 fewer and allowed 4.97 more points a game than its season average.

weekAhead.headline: Four winnable games before the Lakers test the defense
weekAhead.body:
Five games in eight days: at Indiana, a home-and-home with Washington, then Brooklyn and the Lakers at home. Four of the five opponents sit below Atlanta on the site. Indiana (2-5, DRtg 116, 22nd) and Brooklyn (1-5, ORtg 105.9, 28th) are the clearest chances to stop the slide. Brooklyn's 16.3 TOV % (27th) feeds straight into what Atlanta does best.

The Washington pair is the tactical puzzle. The Wizards own the league's best Opp eFG % (48.1) and Opp 3P % (28.7), which is bad news for a team already missing threes. They are also 29th in ORB % and 28th in DRB %, and they barely force turnovers (11.5 Opp TOV %, 29th). Atlanta should win those games on extra possessions and second chances rather than shot-making. The Lakers finish the week as the one team clearly better than the Hawks: first in eFG % and second in FT Rate. Atlanta's rim defense is the worst matchup imaginable for them, but the Lakers also turn it over at a 16.7 TOV % (29th).

keyMatchups.title: Hawks' turnover edge vs Brooklyn
keyMatchups.body: Brooklyn has the 28th-ranked offense and coughs the ball up at a 16.3 TOV %, 27th, while Atlanta forces turnovers at the league's second-best rate. This is the game where the Hawks' identity should produce a comfortable win. Brooklyn has also given opposing power forwards 32.83 points a game, though Atlanta's thin PF rotation may not exploit it.

keyMatchups.title: Crash the glass on Washington
keyMatchups.body: The Wizards' defense smothers shooters, with Opp eFG % first in the league, but they rebound only 68% of opponents' misses (28th). Atlanta's ORB % of 27.2 is middling, so effort on the offensive glass rather than threes is the path in two games that could swing the division race.

keyMatchups.title: Lakers' efficiency vs the open paint
keyMatchups.body: Los Angeles leads the league in eFG % and gets to the line constantly, exactly the kind of offense that punishes a defense ranked last in Opp Rim Rate. Atlanta's counter is the Lakers' 16.7 TOV %. Without a run of live-ball turnovers, expect this one to slip away.

weekAhead.watch: Whether Jalen Johnson plays through his day-to-day status. He leads the team in minutes and assists, and without him the wing group thins to Luguentz Dort, whose BPM is -4.8 and On-Off -21.7.

restOfSeason.body:
With 75 games left, the honest read is a team near break-even. The 82-game pace of 35 wins reflects the recent skid more than the roster. Some things should hold: the turnover margin, which matches the Hawks' history, and the backcourt's quality. The three-point shooting should climb back toward last year's 37.1%, giving the offense a real lift. Working against that, opponents won't keep shooting 32% from three on a defense that concedes this many rim attempts, so the defense likely slides into the bottom half unless the frontcourt improves.

That nets out to a final record in the high 30s to mid 40s, most likely a few games either side of .500. That is play-in territory in an East division where nobody has separated. The upside case is a healthy, bigger frontcourt rotation that cuts off the paint and lets the guard play carry the team back toward last year's 46 wins. The downside is the rim leak and weak rebounding persisting while the turnover edge fades.
swingFactors: Three-point shooting reverting to last year's level

confidence.note: Seven games, one 47-point blowout in the margin, and shooting numbers that swing on a few nights.
